rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent bent mass across all four views, so it clears the basic coherence gate and is not visibly colliding. The dominant gesture is readable, but the form remains fairly compact and generic, with the main weakness being that the road-facing edge does not yet produce a strongly public void or entry seam; the access side feels more sealed than activated. The courtyard/subtractive logic is present in plan, but it is not especially legible as usable public space in elevation/section, so void_publicness and section_program_fit stay modest. Program-wise, the mass can plausibly support neighborhood living/commercial use because it has a manageable scale and a clear main/support relation, but it would benefit from a stronger ground-threshold move and a clearer public opening aligned to the verified frontage. The silhouette is coherent as a single stepped/bent object rather than arbitrary tiering, so it gets a middling-to-good score there, but not a full reward because the section does not yet strongly communicate active public inhabitation.
